title: CFD-003: moving beyond the 20 km/h baseline.
summary: The next prescribed-speed study continues from CFD-002 and begins a 20→30 km/h ramp. Initial motion reversals and the 22.5 km/h marker are recorded, with the run still incomplete.

sections.title: A new question at higher prescribed speed
sections.text: CFD-003 branches from the completed CFD-002 final state. It prescribes a half-cosine boundary-speed increase from 20 to 30 km/h over 0.50 simulated seconds, followed by a planned 0.40 s hold. The target interval is 0.90 s. Surge is constrained; heave and pitch remain free. There is no rider, no jet thrust and the intake is closed. This does not simulate a powered board accelerating under its own propulsion.

sections.title: A dated work-in-progress snapshot
sections.text: The accepted monitoring snapshot is 2026-10-15 03:03:11 UTC. It contains 4,373 synchronized CFD-003 samples through τ003 ≈ 0.231 s at prescribed speed 24.40 km/h. Heave is approximately +83.17 mm from the original CFD-002 release reference, and pitch 10.427° absolute bow-up. The ramp is still active; the planned 30 km/h hold has not been reached.

sections.title: The first speed marker and motion reversals
sections.text: At the interpolated 22.5 km/h marker, τ003 ≈ 0.166667 s, heave is approximately +84.590 mm and pitch 10.360° bow-up. The monitor confirms an early heave maximum near +96.215 mm, a later pitch minimum near 10.293° and a heave minimum near +82.612 mm. Crossing estimates use saved brackets and five consecutive samples on each side. These are transient local reversals, not established cycle amplitudes or settled trim.

sections.title: Continue the accepted trajectory
sections.text: An earlier storage-protection stop and authorized checkpoint continuation are preserved in the run provenance. The continuation retained the original ramp origin and endpoint; it did not restart the speed schedule from zero. Restart continuity and actual boundary-velocity checks passed. The failed initialization attempt occurred before a time step and is excluded from accepted trajectory interpretation.

sections.title: What we cannot conclude yet
sections.text: At a changing prescribed speed, the motion contains the inherited CFD-002 transient and the response to the new boundary condition. The first lower heave/pitch values do not establish better stability, reduced drag at equilibrium or a safe operating limit. Initial mesh concavity flags remain a qualification. Higher-speed comparisons need the completed ramp/hold record, numerical review and eventual physical validation.

sections.title: The next evidence
sections.text: The planned review will compare the remaining speed markers, ramp and hold statistics, corresponding motion excursions and actual saved flow fields. No heavy flow-field rendering or reconstruction was performed for this journal update while the solver is active. The earlier CFD-002 entries remain the comparison record; no new geometry or numerical changes were made for this publication.
